private_watchlist.name: Blue Origin
private_watchlist.note: Root cause of the May 28 New Glenn pad explosion (a BE-4 main oxygen valve) remains under remediation at ULA's Decatur plant and Cape Canaveral, with NASA Stennis hot-fire testing set to begin this fall. Building out Pad 36A plus a second Cape Canaveral pad (36B), a new Vertical Integration Facility, and a government-partnered Payload Processing Facility for the larger New Glenn 9x4. Company remains "very committed" to a return to flight by year-end.

private_watchlist.name: Firefly Aerospace
private_watchlist.note: Reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $117.7M (+659% YoY, first quarter above $100M) on a record $1.5B backlog, alongside a $92.3M net loss; quarter included a $144M NASA CLPS lunar-lander award, a $75M NASA JPL MoonFall subcontract, and a $94M Space Force radar-digitization contract. Roth Capital cut its price target to $45 from $60 on Aug 17 despite the record print; shares down ~28% over the past month on valuation/execution concerns.

private_watchlist.name: Stoke Space
private_watchlist.note: Targeting a close this month on its $1B round (Bloomberg, Aug 13) at a ~$9B valuation ex-new-money, on top of the $1.34B already raised; expanding test facilities at Moses Lake (324 acres) and activating Cape Canaveral's LC-14; first Nova liftoff still targeted for end of 2026.

bear_case.title: Capital intensity
bear_case.description: Rockets and constellations burn billions before returns — Stoke Space is targeting a close this month on its $1B raise on top of $1.34B already spent pre-launch; dilution is chronic among small caps (RKLB's $3.6B Iridium bridge facility, ASTS's $1B convertible notes).

bear_case.title: Government concentration
bear_case.description: Much of the sector's revenue is NASA/DoD — the SDA's Golden Dome build-out (L3Harris/Sierra Space's $1.75B Tranche 3 award, RKLB's $981M NITE-STAR ceiling) keeps flowing, but a CEO ouster at prime contractor L3Harris is a reminder that governance risk sits alongside budget risk in this concentrated customer base.

bear_case.title: SpaceX absorbs the value / sector repricing
bear_case.description: A dominant incumbent with launch-cost leverage can compress everyone else's margins — SPCX dipped back below its $135 IPO price around the Aug 20 share unlock and remains ~39% below its post-IPO high. More broadly, record fundamentals across RKLB, RDW, LUNR and FLY this earnings season haven't stopped a growth-stock/space-stock selloff that's pulled RKLB over 50% off its 52-week high — a widening gap between operating results and price that cuts both ways.

bear_case.title: Binary mission risk
bear_case.description: One failed test or launch can halve a small-cap, or push a manifest a year: Rocket Lab's Neutron — already delayed once by a tank failure, then flagged again by Bloomberg on Aug 10 — still hasn't flown, while Blue Origin's BE-4 root-cause finding shows how fast hardware failure can stall a program ahead of its promised year-end return to flight. SpaceX's own prospectus flags "key man" dependence on Elon Musk.

positions.name: Rocket Lab
positions.note: Fresh $981M NITE-STAR onboarding (Aug 17) and a $12M Space Data Network award (Aug 18) extend the government-revenue base, but the stock kept sliding through the month — down to the low-$70s by Aug 21-23 versus a $151 52-week high — even as Citizens reiterated Outperform/$130 (Aug 11) calling Neutron "derisked"; shares are now trading near the $67.50 floor of the Iridium deal's exchange-ratio collar. Trimming slightly given the price hasn't stabilized and Neutron's year-end debut remains unproven.

positions.name: L3Harris
positions.note: FY26 guidance held and no financial/accounting issues were flagged, but the Aug 17 ouster of CEO Chris Kubasik over a conduct violation — with ~$45M of forfeited equity — is a real governance shock even with a credible internal successor in Sam Mehta (ex-Space & Mission Systems, ~80% of revenue); trimming slightly for leadership-transition risk. Also sits in your Defense sleeve — don't double-count the exposure.

positions.name: Redwire
positions.note: A second straight quarter of records plus continuing Stalker UAS defense follow-ons kept the stock up roughly 38% for August on one tracker; no new catalyst this week either way, so holding steady rather than chasing the rally.

positions.name: AST SpaceMobile
positions.note: BlueBirds 11-13 launched successfully Aug 5 with tech targeting nearly double the peak download speeds of earlier satellites, and the Aug 10 update reaffirmed a ~$1.30B backlog and 60+ MNO partners; still speculative on the $1B convertible overhang and pre-beta commercial status, and shares got caught in the mid-August sector-wide pullback alongside SPCX and RKLB.

positions.name: Intuitive Machines
positions.note: Disclosed a new $600M+ GEO satellite contract (Aug 13, shares +8-17%), was picked for NASA JPL's EAGLE-VSWIR mission, will build 18 IM-1300 platforms for SDA's Tranche 3 missile-defense layer via an L3Harris partnership, and closed the Goonhilly/COMSAT ground-station acquisition — genuine diversification beyond the binary lunar-lander business, so weight moves up even though the book stays lumpy.

positions.name: SpaceX
positions.note: Shares dipped back below the $135 IPO price around the Aug 20 "day 70" unlock of 319M shares before rebounding to ~$137 by Aug 21 — still ~39% below the $225.64 post-IPO high — with four more unlock tranches ahead through Dec 8, 2026. Starship Flight 14 (NET Aug 28) is the next real catalyst: first orbital insertion, first Starlink V3 delivery, and the first tower-catch attempt. UK investors wanting SpaceX exposure without chasing the US listing can get indirect access via Scottish Mortgage (SMT, covered on the Baillie Gifford page).

positions.name: Planet Labs
positions.note: Ten analysts carry a Buy consensus with targets near $34.90-$40 (Aug 20) against a ~$22.35 close — meaningful implied upside on paper — but that's sell-side sentiment, not a company-specific catalyst; no fresh contract or margin news this week to confirm the thesis, so still watch rather than own.

positions.name: Iridium Communications
positions.note: Deal mechanics, not fundamentals, now drive this name: RKLB's S-4 isn't yet effective, the shareholder vote hasn't happened, and RKLB shares trading near the $72-74 low end of the $67.50-$112.50 exchange-ratio collar adds uncertainty to what Iridium holders ultimately receive. RKLB stock remains the cleaner way to express the same view.
